item.title: Wakayama Castle: Stronghold of a Tokugawa Branch — Guide
item.description: Wakayama Castle stands on Torafusu Hill in the middle of the prefectural capital, founded in 1585 by Toyotomi Hidenaga, brother of Hideyoshi, and later the seat of the Kishu Tokugawa — one of the three branch families of the shogunal house, from which the eighth shogun Yoshimune came. Its keep was destroyed in the war and rebuilt in concrete in 1958, but the extensive stone walls, gates and the winding hilltop layout remain impressive, and the Nishinomaru garden below, with its pond, teahouse and vermilion Ohashi covered bridge, is one of the finest in the region.

item.title: Kakegawa Castle: Japan's First Authentically Wooden-Rebuilt Keep — Guide
item.description: Kakegawa Castle, a compact hilltop castle on the old Tokaido highway between Edo and Kyoto, was rebuilt in 1994 as Japan’s first castle keep reconstructed authentically in wood using traditional methods, rather than the concrete used at most modern reconstructions. The site also preserves its original goten palace building, one of only a handful of surviving castle palaces in Japan, giving visitors a rare combination of a faithful wooden keep and genuine Edo-period administrative halls in one visit.

item.title: Yokote Castle: Hilltop Keep & Kamakura Views — Akita Guide
item.description: Yokote Castle is a reconstructed hilltop keep overlooking the town of Yokote in southern Akita, a pleasant viewpoint over the Yokote basin. It’s especially atmospheric in February, when the town below hosts its famous kamakura snow-hut festival and the castle looks out over a snowbound landscape. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Yokote, Akita Hours Keep ~9:00–16:00 (seasonal) Admission Around ¥300 Time needed About 40 min Best time February (kamakura); spring cherries What to See The reconstructed hilltop castle keep and viewpoint.
